speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you have a pruritic rash on both of your upper arms. To help me understand what is causing this, could you tell me how long you have had the rash and if it itches more at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the chronic nature and lack of triggers are helpful. Does the rash appear as small, flat-topped bumps that might be slightly purple or brown, and do you notice it on your ankles or elbows as well? Also, have you noticed any nail changes like pitting or discoloration?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lichen Planus. The chronic, pruritic, bilateral upper extremity rash combined with the absence of systemic symptoms and lack of new triggers is highly suggestive of this condition, even without explicit confirmation of the classic "purple, polygonal, planar, pruritic, and palpable" features or nail changes in your description.
